source.title: Hydrogen refuelling station calibration with a traceable gravimetric standard
source.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article license observed in Crossref/Elsevier metadata)

access_recheck.recheck_note: The public article and project pages expose methods, ranges and aggregate accuracy findings; no downloadable synchronized station-to-vehicle logger archive was identified.

observed_scope.protocol_context: SAE J2601 fuelling conditions are referenced for 700 bar HRS operation.
observed_scope.reference_standard: Traceable gravimetric standard used for on-site comparison/calibration of HRS flow metering.
reported_findings: Repeatability was reported for the tested HRS configurations.
Systematic mass-measurement errors can arise from pressure differences and dead volume between the Coriolis flow meter and the dispenser transfer point.
The flow-meter installation configuration and ambient conditions affect measurement stability and uncertainty.
missing_full_loop_channels: machine-readable synchronized vehicle/receptacle pressure and temperature rows
station controller/PLC state and valve/ESD transitions
cascade-bank, compressor and dispenser state timeline
reusable event-level logger archive with a frozen channel dictionary

allowed_use: mass-flow meter bias and uncertainty sanity checks
SAE J2601 operating-range and pre-cooling boundary context
pre-registration of a station metrology sub-analysis
prohibited_use: reconstruction of raw time-series rows from article figures

claim_boundary: This is real HRS field metrology evidence for the flow-measurement component. It strengthens calibration and uncertainty provenance but does not provide an independent synchronized station-to-vehicle logger archive and cannot close the IJHE full-loop or SAGA-effectiveness gates.
